newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU soft drinks industry seeks sugar regime reform.
newsitem.headline: EU soft drinks industry seeks sugar regime reform.

text.p: The European Union should reform its sugar regime to cut the cost of the product, European soft drinks manufacturers said on Monday.

In a statement timed to coincide with the start of the World Trade Organisation ministerial meeting in Singapore, UNESDA (Union of Soft Drinks Associations) said the regime was incompatible with the GATT (General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade).
It claimed that costly surpluses put the cost of sugar in the EU among the highest in the world.

UNESDA denied that the present regime was self-financing and said it cost the consumer 35 per cent of the retail price of sugar. The five million tonnes of sugar exported with subsidies each year depressed world prices and increased the gap between world and domestic prices, creating a need for more subsidies.
A European Commission official said the regime had been reformed and was compatible with the GATT.
